condition: New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate
summary: 68-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes: 2 days of palpitations and mild exertional breathlessness; irregularly irregular pulse 138, BP 126/84. CHA2DS2-VA 3.

inputs.hpi: Referred for an inguinal hernia. Mentions two days of a fast, irregular heartbeat and getting breathless on the stairs. No chest pain, no blackouts. Drinks 3-4 beers at weekends. Hypertension and type 2 diabetes. No previous stroke.

exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 138 irregularly irregular, BP 126/84, JVP not raised, no murmur.

inputs.socialHistory: Ex-smoker. Alcohol about 12 units a week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: New-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: New atrial fibrillation, rate 138, haemodynamically stable, onset about 48 hours; CHA2DS2-VA 3. Same-day ED/medical assessment; defer hernia surgery.

guideline.name: 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation
guideline.section: AF-CARE: 12-lead ECG to confirm AF; emergency electrical cardioversion for haemodynamic instability; rate control (beta-blocker, diltiazem/verapamil, digoxin); stroke risk with CHA2DS2-VA - oral anticoagulation recommended for score >=2 and considered for 1; DOAC preferred over VKA; look for precipitants (thyroid function, infection)
guideline.citation: Van Gelder IC, Rienstra M, Bunting KV, et al. 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation developed in collaboration with EACTS. Eur Heart J. 2024;45:3314-3414.

rationale: Base AF case. PANE has no AF node; the symptom inference does. Web tachycardia prompt fires at HR >110 without fever. CHA2DS2-VA (ESC 2024, sex removed): hypertension 1 + diabetes 1 + age 65-74 1 = 3.
